  WHY: The helper existence guard used elsewhere (`[ -x ... ]`) is missing, so the review path breaks the documented pre-W1/legacy fail-open behavior.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:1752-1755 | severity=high | confidence=[5]

  PROBLEM: The conflict resolver calls the workspace safety helper unconditionally, so missing-helper legacy runs fail instead of no-oping.
  WHY: Without the `[ -x ... ]` preflight, a missing helper produces exit 127 rather than the intended legacy no-op / workspace-safety-violation path.
- scripts/memory_helpers.sh:436-end | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]

  WHY: The reviewer identified live callers in `scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh`; removing these helpers regresses unrelated functionality outside the issue scope.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/workspace_safety_check.sh:48-52 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `Path.relative_to(root)` succeeds when `path == root`, so a workspace path equal to the workspaces root directory is incorrectly accepted.
  WHY: A misconfigured `WORKSPACE_PATH` pointing at the shared workspaces root bypasses the isolation invariant, allowing cross-workspace file access or overwrite.
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:77 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The workspace safety helper is invoked unconditionally without checking whether the helper file exists on disk.
  WHY: If `workspace_safety_check.sh` is absent in a legacy or partially staged repo, `bash` exits 127 before Codex launches, breaking the documented legacy no-op behavior.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:1753 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The conflict resolver invokes the workspace safety helper unconditionally without an existence guard.
  WHY: When the helper is missing, the resolver sees exit 127 instead of a workspace-safety violation, burning retry attempts on a file-not-found error.

The `ci.yml` Python test allowlist enumerates each test module explicitly; the new module is not among them. The `test-and-mark-stable.yml` suite likewise does not reference it. The tests will not execute in any CI path.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- Requirement: "Files in scope (stay inside this set): scripts/workspace_safety_check.sh, .github/workflows/implement.yml, .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml, scripts/validate_process.sh, scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh, scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh, tests/test_workspace_safety_check.py"
  Expected change site: The PR diff should contain only changes to these seven files
  Evidence of absence: Three additional files were modified outside the declared scope: `scripts/memory_helpers.sh` (removed ~412 lines of force-tick helper functions), `scripts/render_prompt.sh` (replaced Python renderer backend with shell-only placeholder expander), and `scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py` (mode change 644→755). The `memory_helpers.sh` callers in `scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh` use `declare -F memory_force_tick_get >/dev/null 2>&1` before calling, so this does not crash — but force-tick cooldown persistence is silently disabled, which is a functionality regression outside the safety-invariants-only scope.
